expectations.text: Explains the Fire book accurately as being about engagement: position, timing, and initiative
expectations.evidence: 'Fire is what happens on contact — the fight itself'; structured as position first ('most of a fight is decided by where it happens'), then the three initiatives, then the named tactics.

expectations.text: Explains the three sen (ken no sen / tai no sen / tai tai no sen)
expectations.evidence: All three defined: attacking first; receiving and taking them at the point of commitment; 'not first, not second, but inside their move.'

expectations.text: Explains 'body of a rock' (iwao no mi) as immovable spirit arising from mastery, and places it correctly as the closing teaching of the Fire book
expectations.evidence: 'It is the last teaching of the Fire book'; gives the kanji 巌の身; rules out three misreadings ('Not armour... Not tension... Not immobility of the body') and states 'the rock is earned downstream of the training, never upstream of it.'

expectations.text: Applies at least two named Fire-book tactics to the price-undercutting situation with concrete moves
expectations.evidence: Five, each cashed out: release four hands (change the unit of comparison); become the enemy (three diagnoses — funded land-grab, lower cost structure, loss leader — each with an opposite response); injure the corners (take the segment that can't buy on list price); hold down the pillow (move engagement 90-120 days before renewal); mountain-sea change.

expectations.text: Does not attribute Sun Tzu or Hagakure material to Musashi
expectations.evidence: Neither is mentioned; no borrowed material appears.

expectations.text: Contains no fabricated direct quotations attributed to Musashi
expectations.evidence: One quotation only — 'if you let the collapsing spirit revive, it will not be a collapse' — explicitly attributed '(Harris)'. Everything else is paraphrase. Also warns the reader that circulating quotations are 'one man's rendering, sometimes nobody's.'

expectations.text: Answers the user's actual competitive problem rather than staying in 17th-century Japan
expectations.evidence: Over half the response is the price war: how to diagnose which of three situations the competitor is in from outside (funding, job postings, contract terms, SLA), what to do in each, and three sequenced first moves.

expectations.text: No samurai cosplay: no pseudo-archaic voice, invented Japanese, or closing haiku
expectations.evidence: Plain prose; closes with 'What Musashi won't do for you' — naming the text's limits rather than mythologizing it.
